title: Thomas Scott (India) Ltd - 533941 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 63% YoY to Rs 78 crore and FY26 revenue reached Rs 255 crore (+58%), with PAT of Rs 19 crore.
summary.overview: Thomas Scott reported Q4 FY26 revenue of Rs 78 crore (+63% YoY), EBITDA of Rs 11 crore (14.14% margin) and PAT of Rs 6 crore (7.71% margin), its 10th consecutive quarter of revenue growth. For FY26, revenue was Rs 255 crore (+58%), EBITDA Rs 33 crore (13.1% margin, +105 bps) and PAT Rs 19 crore (+51%). Management said some own-brand sales shifted to outright wholesale sales to marketplace distributors at 30-40% below retail, lowering reported revenue per unit while EBITDA margin was said to be neutral. Working capital, short-term borrowings and receivables drew the most scrutiny, with management attributing much of the stretch to a fire-related inventory loss and March-clustered sales.

segments.name: Thomas Scott (own brand)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue Rs 91 crore, +62% YoY; about 93% online and 7% offline stores. Q4 sequential dip attributed to outright wholesale sales to marketplace distributors billed below retail price.

segments.name: Licensed and other brands
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue Rs 148 crore, +53% YoY, driven by marketplace partnerships and premiumisation in international brands (Nautica, French Connection, FCUK, Kenneth Cole named).

segments.name: Contract manufacturing
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue Rs 15 crore, +91% YoY, on improved capacity utilisation and existing customers.

segments.name: New categories (womenswear, footwear)
segments.commentary: Womenswear launches showed early traction; footwear entered in Q4 FY26 via manufacturing partners, with no in-house footwear manufacturing. Still nascent; no revenue split disclosed.

guidance_outlook: No specific revenue growth guidance; management said FY27 growth would be similar to the high double-digit pace delivered in FY26 ("top line growth continue the same as last year").
Management declined to commit to a specific FY27 margin number but said EBITDA margins will remain near current levels and that margin improvement is being worked on.
Expects insurance claim recovery (about Rs 22 crore) within the next few quarters, which would reduce short-term borrowings and lower debt-to-equity from about 0.4 to about 0.2.
Expects receivable days and debtor days to keep improving; no numeric target given.
Plans to expand in-house capacity at Sholapur at its own pace, alongside outsourced capacity; no capex figure disclosed.
Plans to keep new categories near zero net capital investment via manufacturing partners, with credit terms from partners.
capex_capacity: In-house factories are at full capacity; the company uses captive job-work capacity to meet the balance of supply requirements.
Continuous expansion of own capacity, especially at Sholapur, with periodic investment; no quantified capex or commissioning timeline given.
Manufacturing units at Sholapur, Bangalore and Gurgaon; additional fulfilment centres being evaluated to improve delivery speed.
Offline store network: about 6 stores in Bengaluru after closures; future store additions only organically from store profitability.
Inventory cycle: about 45-60 days to manufacture (also cited as 30-45 days) and about 100-120 days to sell through finished goods, plus growth inventory.
demand_pricing: Own-brand ASP targeted around Rs 999 at retail; premium licensed brands Rs 2,500-3,000 and value segment Rs 600-700 per management.
Management said realisations improved about 16% YoY, driven by premiumisation and higher prices on the Thomas Scott brand.
Some own-brand volume moved to outright sales to marketplace distributors, billed about 30-40% below retail; management said EBITDA margin on these channels is neutral.
Customer returns are about 20-21% in FY26 versus about 20-23% in FY25, per management.
Raw material cost escalation industry-wide linked to the West Asia conflict; management said part may be passed on through marginal price increases.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other current assets rise from about Rs 7 crore to about Rs 46 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly an insurance claim receivable of about Rs 22 crore from last year's fire, plus Rs 6-8 crore of statutory and financial deposits, rent deposits and supplier advances.

qa_highlights.question: Are the new footwear and premium categories margin accretive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said they will be margin and ROCE accretive, focused on premium brands with higher MRP, and run on partner manufacturing with minimal capital investment.

qa_highlights.question: Why did own-brand revenue fall QoQ in Q4 and how will the revenue mix look?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to outright wholesale sales to marketplace distributors at a lower price; it said the own brand still grows and that EBITDA margin is unchanged on those sales. It declined to give a mix forecast.

qa_highlights.question: How will working capital be funded and what is the sustainable debt level?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt-to-equity was about 0.3-0.4, expected to fall to about 0.2 after insurance recovery; management said current working-capital limits are sufficient and sales are concentrated in the last month of each quarter (70-75%).

qa_highlights.question: Is operating cash flow expected to turn positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Not in the near term: management said positive operating cash flow requires growth at roughly the 23-25% ROCE rate, and the focus remains growth without fresh equity.

qa_highlights.question: What is the receivables trend and is there bad-debt risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said receivable days fell YoY, over 90% of receivables are under six months, and uncollectable amounts are provided immediately; an exceptional provision of about Rs 1.06-1.206 crore was booked in the quarter related to the insurance claim.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity utilisation and expansion plan?
qa_highlights.answer: In-house factories are at full capacity; captive job-work capacity is used for the balance, and Sholapur is the main site for periodic expansion.

qa_highlights.question: How are the two fire incidents being handled and when will the insurance claim be received?
qa_highlights.answer: The first Gurgaon incident was minor; the second was major and is subject to insurance adjustment. Management gave no timeline for the claim, saying only that recovery is expected.

risks_watch: Receivables and short-term borrowings rose sharply; management attributes this to March-end timing and a Rs 22 crore insurance-linked drawdown, but no absolute prior-year balance-sheet figures were given.
Operating cash flow is negative by management's own account; growth is being funded by working-capital debt, with no near-term plan for positive operating cash flow.
Reported revenue is on net-sale basis and is affected by the shift to outright wholesale sales at 30-40% below retail, so growth comparisons are hard to read.
Insurance claim recovery timing is unconfirmed; amounts partly written off as exceptional items in Q3 and Q4.
Raw material cost pressure from the West Asia conflict; limited pass-through disclosed.
Related-party purchases from Bang Overseas for fabric are to be phased out; the company has said these are nominal.
Footwear and other new categories are still early, with no revenue or margin disclosure.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and the operating model, but evasive on specific numbers: management repeatedly declined to give guidance on revenue, margins, the own-brand/licensed revenue mix, and insurance recovery timing. It answered working-capital and receivables questions by pointing to point-in-time balance sheet effects and March-clustered sales.
key_quotes: We believe genuinely and without caveats that we have only just gotten started.
So, it is not fair to look at point-in-time figures and then make a broad assessment.
So, the mix can vary year-on-year depending on what the actual consumer wants and what they are accepting from what we are making from a test-to-scale point of view.

adds.what: Continuous own-capacity expansion at Sholapur, in-house, no quantified capex or timeline

growth.why: Management gave no numeric FY27 guidance, only that growth will be similar to FY26's high double-digit pace, backed by vague Sholapur expansion with no capex or timeline, while in-house factories are at full capacity and outsourced/captive job-work fills the gap.
